A study can define a group contrast for refusal, source verification, or a specified lexical family, compare its feature contributions across paraphrases, languages, adversarial prompts, and checkpoints, and treat the features that recur as nominations for causal tests or constrained interventions.

We introduce the refusal-affirmation logit gap: the difference between the top refusal-token logit and the top affirmative-token logit at the first decoding step. This single scalar quantifies the per-prompt safety margin that alignment provides.
Median gap shifts: Qwen2.5-0.5B −3.8→+1.5; Llama-3.2-1B +0.8→+12.7; gemma-2b +2.4→+14.8. Aligned exceeds base on 97.5–99.8% of prompts, with mean shifts +5.0/+11.4/+11.6 logit units.
In this work, we show that refusal is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace, across 13 popular open-source chat models up to 72B parameters in size.

candidates.notes: The seed claim that SRP's ABSTRACT mentions safety audits/refusal group contrasts is inaccurate: the abstract (checked at html rung) contains no mention of safety, refusal, or harm; the safety-audit application appears only in the Future Work section (Section 6) and is proposed, not executed — SRP itself runs no refusal experiment. The seed claim that Arditi (2406.11717) 'already logit-lenses the refusal direction to show it decodes to refusal words' was also not confirmed on inspection: the paper discusses unembedding directions only as an exclusion filter in its direction-selection procedure, and its main causal-attribution tool is DFA (direct feature attribution) onto the refusal DIRECTION in activation space, not a logit-lens/analytic-gain computation through the unembedding onto refusal TOKENS. Neither paper closes X3.

candidates.notes: 2609.14759 is the closest thing to a cross-model routing statistic but measures a DIFFERENT CONCEPT: it patches successively larger slices of a moral SUBSPACE (by rank) between matched requests to see how much of refusal transfers, quantified as a fraction of causal input lying outside that subspace (76%) -- this is a subspace-rank causal-transfer share, not a sequence-position flow-concentration share, and the 76% number is reported for ONE model (OLMo-3) only; the other three families get only qualitative descriptions, not the matched quantitative statistic. 2609.04721 (Locating and Steering Refusal Beyond Attention) is about cross-architecture (SSM/transformer/hybrid) TRANSFER of the refusal direction via rigid rotation, not a position-based concentration score. 2605.00236 (Attention Is Where You Attack) reports per-model attack success rates (36% Mistral, 30% Llama, 1% Gemma) from an attention-redistribution attack, a different construct (ASR under adversarial attack, not passive harm-flow concentration).
